title: Vendor Entanglement Risk Index and Tactical Playbook for Model Supply Shocks
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Objective: build a quantitative Vendor Entanglement Risk (VER) index and an operational playbook that triggers pre-approved mitigation actions when model supply or quality signals indicate elevated risk. Scope covers third-party open models and managed endpoints we surface in the Redwood catalog (hosted, dedicated, private).

Why: recent transient outages and sudden deprecations across model providers expose customers to availability and quality regressions. Product needs an automated, explainable signal-to-action layer so platform, procurement, and customer success can react before customer-facing incidents or SLA breaches.

Primary deliverables: 1) VER index definition and scoring algorithm (single scalar 0-100). 2) VER dashboard in Market Signals space with time-series and contributor breakdowns. 3) A graded mitigation runbook (green/amber/red) mapping index thresholds to actions: routing policy changes, pre-warmed reserve provisioning, customer comms templates, procurement triggers for Dedicated capacity, and technical fallbacks (quantized variant rollouts). 4) Integration spec for Redwood Console alerts and PagerDuty playbook hooks. 5) A lightweight experiment plan to validate thresholds using historical outage and synthetic failure injection.

Signal inputs and rationale: availability incidents (historical downtime and time-to-recover), release cadence volatility (breaking changes / deprecations), community engagement (commit frequency, issue backlog), licensing churn risk (public announcements / licensing changes), performance drift (latency P95 increases, error rate), hardware/quantization compatibility (supported quant formats / GPU affinity), regional capacity gaps (region-by-region capacity score), and pricing shocks (list-price changes, spot-market behaviors). Each signal normalized to a 0-1 band then weighted. Proposed starting weights: availability 0.30, performance drift 0.20, licensing 0.15, compatibility 0.10, community 0.10, regional capacity 0.10, pricing 0.05. We will validate weights with historical backtesting and adjust.

Decision thresholds (initial): VER < 30 = green (monitor), 30-60 = amber (preemptive ops playbook: warm compatible model variants, enable auto-fallback routing), > 60 = red (activate procurement/contract escalation, embargo new customer onboarding to affected model, notify key customers). Thresholds are staged and will be tuned during the validation sprint.

Stakeholders: PM (Sofia Chen, product lead), Platform Reliability (Marcus Alvarez), Research/Applied ML (Dr. Lina Park), Procurement (Helena Ortiz), Solutions Eng / CSM triage leads (Jamal Reed).

Success criteria: index reliably predicts known past incidents (precision >= 0.7 at amber+), reduction in mean time to mitigation from detection (target 40% reduction), playbook actions successfully executed for 3 simulated shocks during experiment window, and positive feedback from at least two enterprise customers on proactive comms during a pilot.

Notes/constraints: some signals rely on externally accessible metrics (e.g., provider commit cadence) and may be noisy. We will keep an uncertainty band and expose contributor-level explanations in the dashboard. Integration with private deployments must avoid exfiltrating log-level customer data; only aggregated signals used for VER.

Next steps: Align on signals and weights with Eng/Research by 2025-02-20; build initial ETL for signal collection (ENG-2345) and prototype dashboard wireframe (PM-271001); run backtest using 18 months of historical events; schedule tabletop warroom to validate playbook responses and communications flows.
